links.reason: Kural 1302 measures sulking only by taste (மிக்கற்றால் நீள விடல்), while Akananuru 316 names what the excess costs: செய்யோள் நீங்க, cooking a little food alone, sons at திரங்குமுலை. The pair shows the Kural's 'a little too much' turned into a household's ruin. The note's claim that the Kural's speaker is the friend comes from tradition, not the couplet.

The shared phrase புறப்புண் நாணி and வடக்கிருத்தல் tie the two poems to one death; 65 mourns it as a country stopping (five மறப்ப), and 66 tells the victor வென்றோய், நின்னினும் நல்லன் அன்றே. That the vanquished is ranked over the victor to his face is learned only from the pair. Venni is named in 66; in 65 it comes from the colophon.

Both akam poems name Karikal and வெண்ணி: 246 measures gossip by the roar at Azhundur (அழுந்தூர் ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே), 55 sets the mother's life against the சான்றோர் who died with Cheralathan (அவனொடு செலீஇயர்). One public battle is drawn from the winner's side for scorn and the loser's side for grief. 'A death beyond comfort' is loose: 55's point is the followers who went with him.

The dusk catalogue and the anril at the palmyra's inner frond (பெண்ணை அகமடல் சேர / அகமடல் அகவ) are truly shared. But the quoted lines of Kurinjippattu contain no promise of marriage, and their own dusk is menacing too (சினைஇய வேந்தன் செல்சமங் கடுப்ப), so the claimed contrast of promise and dread fails.

The epithet is shared (தீஞ்சுளைப் பலவின் நாஞ்சிற் பொருநன் / தடவுநிலைப் பலவின் நாஞ்சில் பொருநன்), a real link. But nothing in 380 refers to 140's elephant gift; that the anecdote 'supplies the deed' behind 380 and that his fame 'rested on a story bards shared' is conjecture. The note also passes over 140's colophon naming ஆய் அண்டிரன், not the Nanjil chief.

Kural 233 says nothing but புகழ் stands பொன்றாது; 231 concedes the pyre everything, small (குறுகுக) or sky-high (நீள்க), and denies it only புகழ் மாயலவே. Rule and its instance at the pyre: the pair shows the body burning while the fame the maxim excepts stands.

Aay is named in both (ஆஅய் அண்டிரன் / ஆஅய் கானம்), a real puram-name link, and 152 uses his forest's bamboo for her shoulders. But nothing dates 152 after Aay's death, so 'outlived him as a landmark' is unsupported. The note's 'gives elephants' is also a stretch: in 152 மாஅல் யானை can be Aay's epithet and what he 'scatters' to fill the pit is not named.

The figure ஓர்எயில் மன்னன் against crowned kings is truly shared. But 338 shows no siege and no sleepless watch, only kings bringing gifts (தரினும்) and the father's refusal, so it cannot show 'where the akam poet's image came from'. The siege (ஒருங்குஅகப் படுத்த) and the துயில்துறந்தனள் are 373's alone.

176 names பாரி பறம்பிற் பனிச்சுனைத் தெண்ணீர், and 109 makes those springs like the stars (மீன் கண் அற்று அதன் சுனையே), so the image is truly shared. 176 does not extend 109's siege argument, though. It borrows the famous springs for a simile of neglect by neighbours (ஓரூர் உண்மையின் இகழ்ந்தோர்). As same_image the link is sound.

10 has the Kural's procedure (ஒப்ப நாடி அத்தக ஒறுத்தி; slanderers not believed) and then adds what 541 does not address: தண்டமும் தணிதி for one who comes and holds the feet. The mercy follows the verdict and is earned by submission, so 'mercy after the verdict, not favour within it' is a fair, specific reading of the pair.

The gesture is shared exactly (சிறிய இறைஞ்சினள் தலையே / நோக்கி இறைஞ்சினாள்). But 230 never says the man cannot read it. His பெரிய எவ்வம் may be love-pain after parting, and she checks her tears (பனிவரல் ஒடுக்கி). So 'unreadable' and 'a reading made after the fact' rest on the marker's interpretation, not on the Tamil.

Both hinge on the same supposition (செய்யா உலகத்து நுகர்ச்சி இல்லெனின் / மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும்). The Kural stops there (ஈதலே நன்று), while 214 falls back to மாறிப் பிறப்பின் இன்மை and then fame like a Himalayan peak. Two distinct answers to doubt about the next world are shown.

Kural 745 defines a good fort as one with stored food (கொண்டகூழ்த்தாகி), but 44's fort is one where that has failed: unfed elephants, babies without milk (பாலில் குழவி), houses without water. 44 shames the king's hiding (ஒருசிறை ஒடுங்குதல்), not the fort, so the two do not judge one thing incompatibly. The 'tension' needs the note's own hedged reading.

159 accepts even a kunri's worth if given உவந்து and refuses an elephant given grudgingly (தவிர்ந்துவிடு பரிசில் கொள்ளலென்), so a glad giver makes asking acceptable. Kural 1061 takes exactly that best case (கரவாது உவந்தீயும்) and still ranks not asking far above it (இரவாமை கோடி உறும்). That is a genuine, specific difference in where dignity is drawn.

78 names பாரி with வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன், years of holding out, and kings driven off (ஏந்துகோட்டு யானை வேந்தர் ஓட்டிய). 109 is Kapilar's own speech to the besieging kings (மூவிரும் முற்றினும்). The akam poet uses that settled fame for the fragrance of Pari's pool on the girl's brow, and the note says so.

Kural 81 makes household life exist for விருந்தோம்பல். 395 shows the master handing the guest to the mistress (பொன்போல் மடந்தையைக் காட்டி 'இவனை என்போல் போற்று'), so hospitality is lodged in the house itself, which lasts even in drought (lines 33-38). This rule-and-instance pairing is specific.

Both are Kapilar's friend speaking to the hill lord, but the 'sequence' depends on the colophons. 12's day-trysts-stopped (செறிப்பு) is in its thurai, while the poem only shows the parents' care (கண்ணினும் கடுங் காதலள்). 18 is not built toward marriage: it moves the meeting to day (பகல்நீ வரினும் புணர்குவை).

Both belong to the laments around a king's fast, but 218 names no one, and its maxim is about kind (சான்றோர் சான்றோர் பாலர்), not number. 219's பலரால் ... குறிஇருந்தோரே is itself uncertain. The claim that the laments make the number who joined the measure of worth is not in 218.

Both men argue with a wealth-bent heart, and both roads have killers. But 327's killers grieve only for a missed arrow (கோல்கழிபு இரங்கும்) and weigh nothing by what a man carries. Only 337 has the Mazhavar killing on the chance of gold (பொன்னா குதலும் உண்டு), so the teaches sentence rests on one poem, and the shared killers are paalai stock.

The wording is almost identical (விண்பொரு நெடுங்குடை ... தேர் மோரியர் ... திகிரி திரிதர குறைத்த அறை), a distinctive shared memory. 69 uses the cut rock to say how far he has gone (அறைஇறந்து அகன்றனர்), and 175 sets the sun's orb at that pass as a figure for steady protection of many (பலர்புரவு எதிர்ந்த). The note states both uses correctly.

45: the fight will give மெய்ம்மலி உவகை to other kings; 58: if you do not break your உடனிலை, the earth is yours, and you must ignore the ஏதில் மாக்கள் who would come between you. One calculation of outside profit is stated from division and from union. 45 is a quarrel within one house (both wear ஆர்), not 'between crowns', a small looseness.

Kural 1057 gives the receiver's inner joy at a gift given இகழ்ந்தெள்ளாது. 205 makes the manner a condition, refusing even the three kings' gifts if பெட்பின்றி ஈதல். The move from feeling to rule of acceptance is real and specific.

The shared construction is exact and real: say it to those who can (வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை / ஆற்றுவோர்க்கே). But the teaches sentence conflates two deaths. The Kural's implied death is the woman's, from parting, while 215's killers and vultures threaten the man on the road. The road scene does not make the Kural's threat visible.

Both say give before death (நினக்கும் வருதல் வைகல் அற்றே / நாளைத் தழீஇம் ... படும்), and 359 adds the motive of fame (வசையும் நிற்கும், இசையும் நிற்கும்). That contrast is real. But one quatrain cannot show that 'the later book drops the reward', and the Naladiyar verse does not say that wealth is useless after the drum; it only urges giving now.

The distinctive scene is shared: the calf taken from a grieving cow-elephant and tied in the village (மடப்பிடி இனையக் கன்றுதந்து ... மன்றத்துப் பிணிக்கும் / மடப்பிடி கானத்து அலறக் ... பிணிக்கும்), at Venkatam both times. Since the poems name different lords (Athanungan, Pulli), the scene belongs to the place, as the teaches says. In 389 it is an epithet of plenty; in 83 it is a landmark of distance passed.

Tiger against prey is a generic image. 90 sets it on a herd of deer (மான்கணம்) as one of four rhetorical questions and makes no point about size, while 599's point is bulk and tusks failing (பரியது கூர்ங்கோட்டது ஆயினும்). The teaches sentence only restates that one image serves praise and maxim.
links.text_issue: kural:599 line 2 has a corrupted letter (஦வ்ருஉம் for வெரூஉம்)

links.reason: Two poets' poems on the same paalai situation (wealth journeys) are made into one man's sequence by their colophons. The 'pull outlasting success' comes from 353's thurai alone (பொருண்முற்றி வந்திருந்த காலத்து மீண்டும்), and 351 adds only the return. This is a shared situation, not a development.

The wording is near identical (செய்தி கொன்றோர்க்கு உய்தி இல் / செய்ந்நன்றி கொன்ற மகற்கு உய்வில்லை), and 34 even gives the list of crimes that have expiation (கழுவாயும் உள). 34 turns the rule on the poet (பாடேன் ஆயின்), which the Kural does not, so the pair shows the maxim already binding the bard.

The tension is real: 327 praises the நெடுந்தகை who begs millet (வரகுடன் இரக்கும்) for his kin's want, and 1066 calls asking degrading even ஆவிற்கு நீர். But the teaches turns one pair into a chronology ('a later ethical rule'), which these two verses cannot show. The note's 'to feed bards' is also off: the bards had already eaten, and he begs for his ஒக்கல்.

The two trees are placed differently: the Kural's fruit tree is in the town's heart (உள்ளூர்ப் பழுத்தற்றால்), and 119's is the lone tree on a shadeless road (நிழலில் நீளிடைத் தனிமரம்) for one who gave beyond the kings (வேந்தரை இறந்தும்). The added sense, that worth is measured by the absence of other givers, is a specific gain from the pair.

The two are close in matter (இன்னா ஆகப் பிறர் மண் கொண்டு / அழக் கொண்ட எல்லாம் அழப்போம்). But 12 only asks அறனோ மற்றிது and may be praise, so 'agrees' overstates it. Using the Kural to settle the tone of 12 imports a later answer, and it cannot show what charge the poet's question carried.

The phrase is shared (புதுவது அன்று / சாதலும் புதுவது அன்றே). In 192 the commonplace grounds equanimity toward great and small, and in 76 it is granted only to set off இன்றின் ஊங்கோ கேளலம், one king against seven. A shared formula with opposite ends is shown accurately.

312 divides the duties (ஈன்று புறந்தருதல் என்தலைக் கடனே; சான்றோன் ஆக்குதல் தந்தைக்கு; வேல்வடித்துக் கொடுத்தல் கொல்லற்கு). In 279, with the husband dead yesterday (கொழுநன் ... பட்டனனே), the mother herself gives the spear and sends the only son (வேல்கைக் கொடுத்து ... விடுமே). The breakdown of the division under loss is visible only in the pair.

Both involve a promised quick return ('இன்னே வருதும்' / வல்வரவு), but 229 does not refuse the promise. It reports it broken by the season (இன்இள வேனிலும் வாரார்) and rejects the friend's comfort, whereas the Kural's point is that she will not live to see it. The teaches sentence is only the shared topic of refusing comfort.

The grounds differ as stated: 173 rests on his maxim and gesture (எல்வளை திருத்தினர் ஆயின் வருவர்), 177 on his memory of her body (தொய்யிலை நினைந்தே). But neither limits the other, so qualifies does not fit, and the same comfort office is common akam ground.

Pittan's spear against hostile kings is truly shared (பொருந்தா மன்னர் அருஞ்சமத்து உயர்த்த ... எஃகம் / ஆரமர் கடக்கும் வேலும் ... மாறுகொள் மன்னரும்), and the note says 77 turns it into the wound her eyes give. But the 'great giving' in 172 belongs to his overlord Kothai (அவனிறை மாவள் ஈகைக் கோதையும்), not to Pittan, so note and teaches misattribute it.

The shared image is striking: rags like pond moss replaced with new cloth (முதுநீர்ப் பாசி அன்ன உடைகளைந்து / பகட்டுஇலைப் பாசி வேர்புரை சிதாஅர் நீக்கி). But the father-son relation rests on the colophons (390 names no one), and one poet's repeated motif cannot show an 'inherited house custom'. 390 already speaks of plunder (கொண்டி பெறுக), so 392 does not add conquest.

Both look to death (கணிச்சி ... பிணிக்கும் காலை / நாச்செற்று விக்குள்). The Kural urges hurrying to good, while 195 sets a floor for those who cannot (நல்லது செய்தல் ஆற்றீர் ஆயினும் அல்லது செய்தல் ஓம்புமின்) and counts it as நல்லாற்றுப் படூஉம் நெறி. A genuine limit is added.

110 is Kapilar's own boast to the three kings (பறம்பு கொள்ற்கு அரிதே; யாமும் பாரியும் உளமே). 78 names வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன் beside Pari, who drove the kings off, and uses this for the girl's fragrance. The passage from war-speech to akam reference is shown by the Tamil.

Both have the woman say the rains he named have come without him (காலை வந்தன்றால் காரே / கார்மன் இதுவால்), under paalai and mullai colophons. 183 does dwell on the waste crossed (அத்தம்ஆர் அழுவம்) and 194 on the worked field, so the observation about labels holds. But it is one domain, and parallel_domain does not fit.

Both turn on a spoken promise broken by leaving (பிரியலம் என்ற சொல் / தெளித்தசொல்). The Kural asks about fault (தேறியார்க்கு உண்டோ தவறு), while Akananuru 1 asks only மறந்தனர் கொல்லோ. The contrast between a moral question and a question of memory is real and specific.

Both praise a செழியன் who broke a coalition (இருபெரு வேந்தர் at கூடல் / எழுவர), but the numbers and places differ, and nothing shows it is one king. The note also does not say what Paranar does with it: it is the measure of the gossip's noise (ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே).

The identity of வாட்டாற்று எழினியாதன் with the செல்லிக் கோமான் ஆதன் எழினி rests only on Kosar appearing in both lands. 216's syntax leaves open whether Ezhini struck the elephant or was struck (ஆதன் எழினி அருநிறத்து அழுத்திய). The note reads it one way while the verse's own marking reads it the other, so the 'two reputations' claim rests on two conjectures.

அலர் in 1141 is the public talk about lovers, which keeps the speaker's life. புறங்கூறல் in 183 is malicious backbiting, judged from the backbiter's own life. The verses speak of different acts and different persons, so no incompatible claim exists; only a loose likeness of 'talk' joins them.

poems.note: The thazhai bloom guarded by toothed fronds suggests a guarded girl, but only one correspondence holds and the thurai is about rebutting the companion.
The lone herdsman in the rain night matches the waiting wife only in mood; his acts (fire, whistle, scaring the jackal) are a herdsman's, not hers.

iraicchi.act: the wildcat's kitten keeps to its mother's track through the fearful forest, like stars round the moon
iraicchi.sense: even the forest's young go with their own, so her 'வருவல்' (I will come with you) was right and leaving her behind is what pains him

poems.note: The monkey scene sits inside an open comparison (மாங்காட்டு அற்றே ... தந்தை காப்பே), so it is not hidden.
The north wind is the addressee, so striking it removes the poem.

iraicchi.act: the male wildcat watches for the cock at dusk to end his famished mate's hunger
iraicchi.sense: at evening even the wildcat stays and provides for his mate, while her own partner is away, so the dusk is sweet only for those united

iraicchi.act: the little sea crow rests with its mate on the thazhai and dreams of prawns at midnight
iraicchi.sense: even the crow is with its mate at midnight while she lies alone, sharpening her appeal to the crab to carry word to the lord

ullurai.anchor: இன்னும் பிறள்வயி னானே; மனையோள் எம்மொடு புலக்கும்

poems.note: Two pairs: the tall leaf that sways at every gust is the man who turns to each woman, and the deep pond it stirs is the household his wife keeps; the elephant-ear simile is an open comparison of the leaf only.
Puram poem (perunthinai); both fields null by rule.

ullurai.anchor: ஒலிமணி நெடுந்தேர் ஒள்ளிழை மகளிர் சேரிப் பல்நாள் இயங்கல்
